description: Original 1861 woodcut illustrations from Mayhew's 'London Labour and the London Poor' Vol. II — engraved from daguerreotypes by Richard Beard. All in the public domain. URLs point at Project Gutenberg's scan (ebook 60440). `url` is the display-sized image; `url_hires` is the high-resolution version. Every plate is reproducible — download, self-host, or link directly.
source_edition: Henry Mayhew, 'London Labour and the London Poor' Vol. II (1861 expanded edition).
attribution: Engraved c. 1851 from daguerreotypes by Richard Beard (1801–1885). Public domain (pre-1928 US, pre-1928 UK author d. 1885).

entries.title: The Bone-Grubber
entries.caption: THE BONE-GRUBBER.
entries.description: Man in ragged coat and battered hat with the trade's bag and hooked stick. The archetypal bone-grubber figure Mayhew describes as "covered with bird-lime" from grease and dust.

entries.title: The Mud-Lark
entries.caption: THE MUD-LARK.
entries.description: Boy on the Thames foreshore at low tide, barefoot, with a tin for his finds. The primary visual reference for the three child testimonies in this library.

entries.title: The London Dustman
entries.caption: THE LONDON DUSTMAN.
entries.description: Dustman in fan-tailed hat and leather back-flap, with bell and shoulder-basket. Fan-tail is an occupational identifier visible across the trade.

entries.title: View of a Dust-Yard
entries.caption: VIEW OF A DUST YARD.
entries.description: Panorama of a working dust-yard: sifting gangs (mostly women), piled heaps, carts unloading. Direct visual reference for the Mayhew passage on the ~£147,700 annual dust trade.

entries.title: The London Scavenger
entries.caption: THE LONDON SCAVENGER.
entries.description: Street-cleansing labourer with broom and shovel. The scavenger class is the third tier of Mayhew's finder/collector taxonomy.

entries.title: The Able-Bodied Pauper Street-Sweeper
entries.caption: THE ABLE-BODIED PAUPER STREET-SWEEPER.
entries.description: Workhouse-assigned street labourer — the pauper tier of sweeping, distinct from the independent street-sweeper or the chimney-sweep.

entries.title: The Rubbish Carter
entries.caption: THE RUBBISH CARTER.
entries.description: Cart-driver removing builders' rubbish and house-refuse. Peripheral collector class in Mayhew's scheme.

entries.title: The London Sweep
entries.caption: THE LONDON SWEEP.
entries.description: Adult chimney-sweep with rods and soot-sack. The post-climbing-boy era depicted; the next plate shows a climbing sweep.

entries.title: One of the Few Remaining Climbing Sweeps
entries.caption: ONE OF THE FEW REMAINING CLIMBING SWEEPS.
entries.description: A surviving child climbing-sweep — by 1861 the Act of 1840 had nominally banned the practice; Mayhew's inclusion of this plate is political.

entries.title: The Sweeps' Home
entries.caption: THE SWEEPS' HOME.
entries.description: Domestic interior of a sweep's household — smoke-blackened walls, sleeping children. The domestic counterpart to the occupational plates.

entries.title: The Sewer-Hunter
entries.caption: THE SEWER-HUNTER.
entries.description: ⭐ THE REPO NAMESAKE PLATE. Tosher in long greasy velveteen coat, eight-foot iron-hooked pole over shoulder, lantern hanging from the waist, dirty canvas trousers. The iconic visual record of the trade that gave this library its name.

entries.title: Diagram of the Sewer (cross-section)
entries.caption: Diagram of the [sewer cross-section]
entries.description: Technical diagram of a London sewer in cross-section — used in the engineering portion of the sewerage chapter. Useful reference for any map/game that needs underground geometry.

entries.title: Flushing the Sewers
entries.caption: FLUSHING THE SEWERS.
entries.description: Commissioner workmen releasing water to scour the sewers — the institutional rival to the freelance toshers, who worked the same tunnels illegally.

entries.title: The Rat-Catchers of the Sewers
entries.caption: THE RAT-CATCHERS OF THE SEWERS.
entries.description: Men with dogs and lanterns working a sewer outlet for rats — the predators the toshers feared ("them there water rats … would think nothink of tackling a man"). Directly supports the 06-cuckolds-point-tosher testimony.

entries.title: London Nightmen
entries.caption: LONDON NIGHTMEN.
entries.description: Cesspool-emptiers at work by lantern-light — the other nocturnal trade of the sanitation economy. Worked in teams of four with long-handled shovels and horse-carts.

entries.title: Scene in Petticoat-Lane
entries.caption: SCENE IN PETTICOAT-LANE.
entries.description: Street-scene in the rag-and-old-clothes market quarter. The Petticoat-Lane Jew fence paid the Cuckold's Point tosher £7 10s for the Parliament Houses bracelets; the lane was also HQ for the bone-grubbers.

entries.title: A View in Rosemary-Lane
entries.caption: A VIEW IN ROSEMARY-LANE.
entries.description: Street-scene in the "wretched locality" between the Docks and Rosemary Lane — the pure-finder widow's and the Liverpool bone-grubber's home ground.
